neighbours.label: finance-sense nouns in investment text: a broker's ' commission', a fund's ' return', a firm's ' client', price ' volatility', bonds ' converted'; the same words in non-financial senses (arts commission, return of the swallows) stay quiet
fire: Mutual funds charge an annual fee, and the broker's commission is added on each trade.
Over ten years the index fund delivered an average annual return of six percent.
Investors in emerging markets must accept higher volatility in share prices.
The stockbroker earns a commission whenever an investor buys shares.
The hedge fund reported a net return of twelve percent to its investors.
The investment bank advised its largest client on the bond issue.
Options traders watch implied volatility closely before earnings reports.
The bonds were converted into ordinary shares at a fixed price.
quiet: The city council charges an annual fee, and the planning commission meets each month.
Over ten years the swallows made their annual return to the same barn.
Chemists handling the solvent must respect its high volatility in warm rooms.
The mayor appointed a commission to study the traffic problem.
The tennis star's return of serve was the best in the tournament.
The hairdresser offered her client a cup of tea.
The mood in the stadium changed quickly before the final whistle.
The barn was converted into a small theatre last summer.

notes: Card: ' return' x4, ' client' x4, ' commission' x2, 'vol'(atility), re'ins'urer, all in securities/fund text; the + pole is deal-making (M&A, origination). Probe: broker's commission 0.36, fund's return 0.21, volatility 0.20, client of the law firm 0.04; arts commission 0.01, return of the swallows 0.02.
